name: alfredo
instructions:
ALFREDO. Variant A is the classic — just PARMESAN, BUTTER, and FETTUCCINE, italian style. Variant B is the mushroom version — shittake or chanterelle, lemon juice, garlic, thyme + oregano, and crisped panko/breadcrumbs at the end.

=== VARIANT A — THE CLASSIC (PARMESAN + BUTTER + FETTUCCINE) ===

The original roman dish (Alfredo di Lelio's fettuccine al burro): no cream, no garlic, no flour — the sauce is BUTTER + PARMESAN emulsified with starchy PASTA WATER on the noodles.

SERVES 2.

- 8 oz fettuccine
- 4 tbsp (57g) good butter, cubed
- ~1 cup (80-100g) PARMESAN, finely grated (microplane — fine grate melts evenly)
- salt (lightly — the parmesan is salty)

1. Cook the fettuccine in LESS WATER THAN USUAL (starchier water = better emulsion), lightly salted. Pull it just shy of al dente. RESERVE A CUP OF PASTA WATER.
2. In a warm (not hot) wide pan or bowl, toss the pasta with the butter and a splash of pasta water until the butter melts into a glossy coat.
3. OFF THE HEAT, add the parmesan in stages, tossing vigorously and loosening with pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce is creamy and clings. Same emulsion discipline as [[cacio-e-pepe]] — too much direct heat and the cheese seizes.
4. Serve immediately — the sauce tightens as it sits and does not hold or reheat.

=== VARIANT B — MUSHROOM (SHITTAKE OR CHANTERELLE + LEMON + GARLIC + CRISPED CRUMBS) ===

Variant A's butter-parmesan emulsion, plus:

- SHITTAKE or CHANTERELLE MUSHROOMS, sautéed
- GARLIC
- THYME + OREGANO
- LEMON JUICE
- PANKO or BREADCRUMBS — CRISPED separately and ADDED AT THE END (a crunchy topping, not stirred through)

1. CRISP THE CRUMBS: toast the panko/breadcrumbs in a little butter or oil until golden. Set aside — they go on at the very end.
2. SAUTÉ the mushrooms in butter; add the garlic and the thyme + oregano near the end of the sauté.
3. Build the butter-parmesan emulsion on the pasta as in variant A, fold in the mushrooms.
4. LEMON JUICE to finish.
5. Scatter the crisped crumbs over the top at the end and serve.

=== VARIANT A IS THE REAL ALFREDO — NO CREAM ===

The italian original is a butter-and-parmesan emulsion on fresh fettuccine — the american cream-garlic-flour version is a different dish built on top of the name. Variant A stays italian: butter + parmesan + pasta water, nothing else. (If an americanized cream build ever earns a place here, it comes in as its own variant.)

=== THE EMULSION RULES (SHARED WITH [[cacio-e-pepe]]) ===

Same technique family as [[cacio-e-pepe]]: fine grate, starchy water from a low-water boil, cheese in off the heat, loosen with pasta water in stages. Parmesan is more forgiving than pecorino, which makes alfredo the easier of the two to land.

=== VARIANT B — THE MUSHROOM BUILD ===

Shittake or chanterelle in the mushroom slot; garlic, thyme + oregano in the sauté; LEMON JUICE to cut the butter-parmesan richness; PANKO or BREADCRUMBS crisped separately and added AT THE END so they stay crunchy on top.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[cacio-e-pepe]]: the pecorino + pepper sibling — same emulsion mechanics, sharper cheese, pepper as co-lead.
- [[boscaiola]]: the cookbook's cream-based pasta — where actual cream belongs.
